statTooltips.str: STRENGTH (STR) - Physical power. Determines melee damage and lifting capacity. Roll: 3D6×5
statTooltips.con: CONSTITUTION (CON) - Health and endurance. Determines Hit Points and poison resistance. Roll: 3D6×5
statTooltips.siz: SIZE (SIZ) - Height and body mass. Influences HP and Damage Bonus. Roll: 2D6+6×5
statTooltips.dex: DEXTERITY (DEX) - Agility and coordination. Affects Dodge and combat initiative. Roll: 3D6×5
statTooltips.app: APPEARANCE (APP) - Physical appeal and social poise. Useful in interpersonal encounters. Roll: 3D6×5
statTooltips.int: INTELLIGENCE (INT) - Cognitive ability and reasoning. Determines personal interest skill points. Roll: 2D6+6×5
statTooltips.pow: POWER (POW) - Force of will and spiritual fortitude. Determines starting Sanity and Magic Points. Roll: 3D6×5
statTooltips.edu: EDUCATION (EDU) - Formal schooling and retained lore. Determines occupational skill points. Roll: 2D6+6×5
statTooltips.luck: LUCK - Fortune and providence. May be spent to adjust dice rolls. Roll: 3D6×5

derivedTooltips.hp: HIT POINTS (HP) - Trauma tolerance of the body. When dropped to 0, investigator is unconscious or dead. Formula: (CON + SIZ) / 10
derivedTooltips.san: SANITY (SAN) - Mental stability and equilibrium. Falls upon encountering cosmic horrors. Starting value = POW
derivedTooltips.mp: MAGIC POINTS (MP) - Occult energy reserve. Used to cast spells. Formula: POW / 5
derivedTooltips.damageBonus: DAMAGE BONUS (DB) - Extra melee combat impact. Depends on STR + SIZ
derivedTooltips.build: BUILD - Physical stature rating used for combat maneuvers like shoving. Depends on STR + SIZ
derivedTooltips.movement: MOVEMENT (MOV) - Base walking/running rate. Depends on STR, DEX, SIZ and age

data.background: Mask: A mastered, cynical veteran of the newspaper "The Pall Mall Gazette", a cool analyst of facts and financial plots. Hidden fear: Panic fear of the Thames water and the sound of bubbling under the keel - since the night when his father's fished body lacked heart and internal organs. In stress situations, he reflexively spins a brass watch and nervously cleans his nails from ink.
data.characterConcept: Inquisitive reporter tracking blasphemies hidden under the smooth floor of Victorian salons.
data.ideology: The world is based on lying to rich and police silence. The truth is the only acid that can dissolve this screen.
data.significantPerson: Edward H. Sterling, editor-in-chief of "Pall Mall Gazette" - a strict patron who keeps Arthur's uncensored manuscripts in the safe and protects him from prison.
data.meaningfulLocation: A well-maintained but scented quinine and zecer lead editorial on Fleet Street, where the vibrations of printing machines deafen his nightmares.
data.treasuredPossession: A brass pocket watch from his father with a crooked clue held at 03:17 - in his envelope he hid an encrypted list of names from the lodge at Limehouse docks.
data.description: A thin man with grey skin and mustaches cut with military severity. He wears a worn-out tweed suit stained with black ink and smoldering grease. He speaks with a quiet, matt voice, often interrupting sentences with a quick scraping of a pencil in a notebook.
data.backstory: For fifteen years, Arthur documented criminal chronicles in the London East End, becoming an informal underground archivist. His faith in the power of the word broke that night when his father's body was taken out of the waters of the Thames—or rather the heartless and gutless shell. In the brass envelope of the father's watch, whose netted clues stopped at 3:17 p.m., Arthur found a list of encrypted the names of the members of the Marine Lodge from Limehouse docks. From that day on, he has been terrified of the cloudy waters and the sound of bubbling. Only a strict editor, Edward Sterling, protects him from madness or imprisonment. Arthur still wears a worn-out tweed smelling of ink and zecer lead, and working in the editorial office on Fleet Street regains his calmness, as the noise of printing machinery effectively deafens his nightmares. Tracking blasphemous cults lurking in Victorian salons, Arthur relies on cool, cynical rationality, believing that the only cure for the rot of this world is to pour it into an objective press form.
data.tacticalNotes: An insightful observer, great in interviews and gossip gathering.
traits: The nervous habit of improving cuffs

data.background: Mask: Discrete, mastered owner of Soho's marriage and investigation office, maintaining cool Victorian stoicism. Hidden Fear: Panic fear of underground crypts and rhythmic tapping into walls - since the day she found her brother's empty clothes in a flooded crypt beneath St. Giles' church. Under stress, it grabs the edge of the corset firmly or improves the rapid movement of the black veil.
data.characterConcept: Independent investigator permeating the dark secret lodges and salons of the London aristocracy.
data.ideology: Men rule the law, but secrets rule the people. If you have a secret, you have real power.
data.significantPerson: The missing brother Thomas Vance - a rose cross researcher whose sudden disappearance left her life with disbelief and rage at the slowness of Scotland Yard police.
data.meaningfulLocation: Hidden room behind a closet on the floor of an office on Greek Street, where he stores drawings of London's underground maps.
data.treasuredPossession: Silver medallion with his brother's photo and a miniature elastic locket hidden in a double bottom.
data.description: A thin woman with strikingly bright gray eyes, creating a contradiction with a raw, dark dress from a cut cloth. He wears a hat with a thick veil of black gipira. He speaks a frugal, exquisite language of aristocracy, concealing under him the knowledge of the flupser of London robbers.
data.backstory: When Scotland Yard shruged his arms in recognition of Thomas Vance's escape as a banal avoidance of creditors, Beatrice abandoned the conventions and entered the shadow world herself. Searching for traces of her only brother in the water-filled catacomb system under St. Giles' church, she found only his empty, panic-forsaken clothes and an encrypted journal full of bizarre descriptions of underground rituals. Today he leads his own detective office under the name of the marriage office in Soho, where he studies the ancient drawing of London's dungeons in a hidden room. Under a dense black veil of gipira and blameless British stoicism, Beatrice hides a panicky fear of the underworld and a deaf rhythm tapping from the crypt walls. He always carries a silver medallion with a picture of Thomas in it, in which he hides a fine but professional locket. To the world she remains a calm and discreet lady of cut cloth; however, in darkness she can talk in the cockney and open every British castle, quietly hoping that one of London's robbers knows the secret to the underworld where her brother can still be buried.
data.tacticalNotes: Perfect for hiding, tracking targets and opening locks.

data.backstory: Zofia spent her entire life in Traszyn, working in a modest municipal library and taking care of a sick aunt who was considered the last rural herbalist and whisperer. Since her youngest years Zosia has absorbed local applications, listing in thick notebooks legends about drownings, bies and forgotten graves in surrounding groves. He remembers the old residents whispering about the tragedy in the old '80s barn when the fun Three children ended in the death of one of them and the deaf silence of the others. When a desecrated, inverted cross was found in the field behind the village, and an inexplicable plague broke out among livestock, Zosia realized that old great-grandmother warnings were not just folk tales. Equipped with a leather songbook full of archaic protective formulas and unparalleled knowledge of rural conexions, Sofia is the only guide to the closed community of Traszyn for visiting researchers. Behind her girlish charm and warm smile, however, lies the constant fear of darkness and the creaking of boards in abandoned homes.
data.tacticalNotes: Focused on research and finding connections to myths. Perfect sense of orientation in gossip.

data.ideology: The truth is often uglier than any bizarre explanation.

data.meaningfulLocation: His playful, smelly old tobacco office.
data.treasuredPossession: Silver flask, always slightly filled.
data.description: The creased Trench and deep bags under your eyes look like a relic of another era.
data.backstory: Arthur is a relic of a long-lost era, a bitter ex-militarian who, after a systemic transformation, opened a one-man detective office in a soul building in Legnica. For decades of service in Lower Silesia, he saw the worst manifestations of human wickedness, corruption and crime. His career with the police broke down in 1991 after an unexplained tragedy in the Glogow underground, where the sent patrol disappeared without a trace, And the only surviving officer fell into irreversible insanity. Since then, Arthur has mostly lived from searching for missing youth and minor divorce cases, drowning memories in a silver flask with rye and burning a pack of cigarettes behind a package. Accepting an order to find a boy connected to a glogow internet cafe was supposed to be a simple job for good money. But when he found The notes on the great simulation and traces of creatures whose bullets don't fit, the old cop had to take off his illegal revolver. In a dented trainer and with a cigarette in the corner of his mouth, Arthur stands for his final investigation, ready to face the truth worse than any crime of militia records.
data.tacticalNotes: Effective in interrogations, looking for physical evidence, and a hard fight with bandits.

data.background: Samouk, who spends nights on the early BBS internet forums. He believes the system we live in is simulation.
data.characterConcept: I'm fascinated by the paranoid computer, willing to believe the machines will take control.
data.ideology: Information must be free, but no one is safe on the network.
data.significantPerson: A user with the nickname "Oracle" with whom he has been correspondence for two years without knowing him personally.
data.meaningfulLocation: Basement with several networked PCs on Windows 95.
data.treasuredPossession: Hard drive filled with encrypted logs from paranormal forums.
data.description: Pale, he drinks a lot of cheap energy drinks. Dressed in too big a hoodie.
data.backstory: For Peter, the outside world was always too loud, chaotic and devoid of logic. As a samouk, he spent his youth in the basements of the family block in Legnica, surrounded by old CRT monitors, network cables and dial-up modem noise. In the world of BBS and IRC channels, he was considered legend of underground hacking, breaking security features for telecommunications systems and university servers. Everything has changed a memorable night, As part of the network push, he hacked into a server connected to the Glogow industrial infrastructure. Instead of standard databases, he intercepted an infinite stream of alien fractal strings that, after decoding, were stacked into error logs in the physical structure of the world around us. Moments later, his mysterious interviewer about Oracle's nickname disappeared from the net, and Peter's apartment was powered down. Pale, sleepless and addicted to cheap energy drinks, Peter does not break up with a heavy laptop and encrypted disk. He is absolutely convinced that the Gloves have become the epicentre of the flaw in the space code, and that the errors of rendering reality will soon lead to the complete reboot of our world.
data.tacticalNotes: It moves perfectly on computers, technology, it can bypass digital security.

data.background: He works at a mental hospital in Legnica. She has recently encountered many cases of sudden derealisation in youth.
data.characterConcept: A compassionate but tired doctor whose scientific foundations are slowly breaking under the pressure of the unexplained.
data.ideology: Every headache has a chemical background - until it is known that it is the influence of nightmares from the outside.
data.significantPerson: Her patient, Zero, who, before falling into a coma, talked about a "net in the sky."
data.meaningfulLocation: A terrorized, suffocating unit locked in, where he spends days and nights.
data.treasuredPossession: Notebooks of the most cumbersome treatment cases.
data.description: She wears an elegant white coat on a straight blouse, her posture suggests immense stress fatigue.
data.backstory: Dr. Krystyna Zawada led a closed psychiatric hospital ward in Legnica for almost three decades. As a dry clinicist, she has always felt that every hallucination, hallucination, or delusion have their hard roots in brain neurochemistry. This unbreakable certainty fell into the rubble of one night of the turn of the millennium, when three totally alien teenagers from Glogow were brought to her ward. Young People They were in a state of deep shock, repeating in a trance the same mathematical sequences and speaking of the fading sky above the city. Worse still, on each of them, Krystyna discovered identical geometric burns resembling traces of integrated circuits. Trials of conventional therapy failed, and one of the patients warned the doctor about the coming matter decay before falling into coma. Always mastered, dressed in a pristine white coat and with a clinical notebook under your armpit, Krystyna decided to go to Glogow personally. Behind her cold professionalism lies the growing fear and determination to save her patients from a nightmare beyond the framework of modern medicine.
data.tacticalNotes: First aid, stabilizing team mentality, in-depth witness psychoanalysis.

data.background: Editor of "Fourth Dimension" niche magazine. He travels Poland with magnetic anomalies detectors in search of alien traces.
data.characterConcept: An irreconcilable, passionate woman believing that the government is hiding the existence of alien civilizations from us.
data.ideology: Both the gods and the demons are simply visitors from other stars our mind is not yet grasping.
data.significantPerson: Her partner, with whom they used to run a canal until he disappeared while searching for crop circles.
data.meaningfulLocation: Her mangled motorhome, covered with aluminum foil and pictogram maps.
data.treasuredPossession: An unusual crystal supposedly found at the site of the plane crash.
data.description: He wears hippie clothes, a lot of bracelets and always with a camera on hand.
data.backstory: Karolina is an untiring searcher of truth about extraterrestrial civilizations and anomalous phenomena in Poland in the 1990s. Since her partner's mysterious disappearance during the expedition to the famous crop circles near Wylatow in 1997, her home has become a crumpled motorhome covered with aluminium foil and pictogram maps. As an independent magazine publicist, the Fourth Dimension traveled across the country with photo cameras night and homemade electromagnetic field detectors. When her sensors registered giant radiation disturbances and microwaves emanating from the abandoned corridors under Glogow, she immediately directed her car there. Carolina believes that what the ancient people called gods and demons, and today they consider to be visitors from outer space, is an ancient intelligence operating on the higher frequencies of the universe. Stubborn, passionate and fearless in the face of the unknown, with the inherent camera in her hands, Luna is ready to enter the deepest underground to gain hard evidence that humanity has never been alone on this planet.
data.tacticalNotes: As a field researcher with a large MOC she is great at operating at the interface of myths, occultism and observation.

StepUploadRulebook.starterText: d100 Core Rules. The core rule is a K100 (d100) roll against a character's skill or characteristic. A roll equal to or below the value is a success. samples.title: First meeting with Professor Armitage
samples.content: Professor Armitage seemed deeply worried. He spoke of strange events at the Miskatonic library. He mentioned missing books and odd sounds coming from the basement. His hands trembled as he showed me the yellowed pages of Wilbur Whateley's journal.

samples.title: Discovery in the library basement
samples.content: In the basement we found strange symbols on the walls. They looked very old, probably from the time the university was founded. Dr Knox recognized some of them as originating from ancient cults.

samples.title: Night visit to Innsmouth
samples.content: I will never forget what I saw on the waterfront. Figures scurrying between warehouses, their strange shambling gait. The smell of salt water and something... rotting. The locals glared at me with hostility, and their eyes... God, those eyes were too large, too fish-shaped.

samples.title: Letter from Doctor Morgan
samples.content: I received a disturbing letter from Dr Morgan of the Arkham sanatorium. He writes about a patient who speaks in an unknown language and draws on the walls the same symbols we saw in the basement. The patient claims that "They are coming from the stars" and that "the gates shall open". I must visit him.

samples.title: Ancient ritual near Bolton
samples.content: Following the clues from Whateley's journal, we reached a stone circle in the hills near Bolton. The signs on the stones pulsed with a faint greenish light as dusk fell. One of us fainted and talked in his sleep in a language no one could recognize. We must return at the full moon.

samples.title: Mystery of the town hall clock
samples.content: The locals say the old clock in the town hall tower stopped at exactly 3:33 at night, when Mayor Harrington disappeared. Since then no one dares repair it. I have heard strange sounds coming from the tower - as if someone were walking there in the middle of the night.

samples.title: The interrogation of Joseph Curwen
samples.content: Joseph Curwen, an antiquarian from Salem, agreed to answer our questions. His shop was full of dusty tomes and strange artefacts. When I asked about the Necronomicon he went pale and ordered me out at once. Before the door closed behind me he whispered: "Some knowledge costs more than reason."

samples.title: Dream of R'lyeh
samples.content: For the third night in a row I dreamt of the sunken metropolis. Cyclopean walls of dark stone, impossible angles of architecture that hurt my eyes. At the end I always see IT - something vast waiting in the darkness of the sea depths. I wake up screaming and cannot stop thinking of the words: "Ph'nglui mglw'nafh Cthulhu R'lyeh wgah'nagl fhtagn."

CompendiumModal.app_journalStep2Desc: Expand completed scene summaries to review persons, acquired items, and deduction leads.

CompendiumModal.app_chatStep1Desc: Write or speak what your hero sees, feels, and attempts in the game world fiction.

CompendiumModal.app_diceStep1Desc: When the Keeper asks for a roll, click the in-chat button or open the dice tray.

CompendiumModal.rp_fictionFirstDesc: First describe your character's intent, senses, and physical actions in the world, then roll dice. Don't announce a check – describe an action.
CompendiumModal.rp_failForwardDesc: A failed check never stalls the plot. It is not an empty miss, but a tense complication or a clue obtained at a perilous cost.
CompendiumModal.rp_somaticDesc: Mention dry throats, the smell of mothballs, shaking hands, or damp chill. These cues instantly elevate the Keeper's prose.
CompendiumModal.rp_duetDesc: When playing as a pair, confer openly, coordinate collaborative tactics, and switch active investigators in the chat header.
CompendiumModal.rp_contrastHeader: Chat Contrast – Witness the Immersion Difference
CompendiumModal.rp_contrastExplanation: The Keeper of Secrets AI mirrors your prose style. Notice how the same goal approached with two styles transforms the Keeper's reply:
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_door_conciseResponse: You press the handle, but the lock holds tight. Stale chill seeps past the timber. What do you do?
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_door_immersivePrompt: I lean my shoulder against the cold wood, resting my hand on the iron latch while straining to hear if anything is shuffling below.
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_door_immersiveResponse: Iron chill bites through your leather glove. Through warped floorboards comes the rank stench of mold and mothballs. As you lean in, something heavy thuds on stone far below, followed by suffocating silence. The door is barred from within with a heavy bolt. [What do you do?]
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_search_concisePrompt: I search the professor's desk for documents.
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_search_conciseResponse: Inside the drawer lies a folder of notes and a newspaper clipping from 1926.
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_search_immersivePrompt: With trembling fingers I sift through scattered manuscripts, checking for traces of the dark ink the archivist warned about.
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_search_immersiveResponse: Dust drifts through amber lantern light. Amid Latin botanical treatises you find a yellowed folder bound with faded ribbon. Nervous notes in purple ink scrawl across the margins, and fresh ash in the inkwell proves someone burned letters barely fifteen minutes ago. [What do you do?]
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_npc_concisePrompt: I ask her what she saw last night.
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_npc_conciseResponse: The woman weeps, saying she heard strange howling coming from the woods.
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_npc_immersivePrompt: I hand her a mug of hot tea, sit across from her and speak gently: 'Mrs. Hudson, you are not alone. Tell me about the sound at three o'clock.'
CompendiumModal.rp_scenario_npc_immersiveResponse: Her knuckles whiten around the steaming porcelain, spilling tea onto her apron. She lifts bloodshot eyes wide with terror. 'That was no beast, sir... Wolves don't scratch on upstairs windows. It... it whispered my maiden name.' The grandfather clock in the hallway strikes a single metallic chime. [What do you do?]
CompendiumModal.rp_conciseOutcomeNote: The action is valid and advances the plot in an economical tone.
CompendiumModal.rp_immersiveOutcomeNote: The Keeper picked up sensory cues, delivering rich atmosphere and plot hooks.
CompendiumModal.rp_goldenRuleBody: Neither style is wrong. If you are short on time, write concisely. If you want deep cosmic dread – enrich your prompt with senses.

CompendiumModal.lore_ruleSuccessLevelsSummary: Two d10 dice (tens and units) matched against your investigator's skill rating.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleSuccessLevelsMechanics:
• Regular Success: roll ≤ skill value.
• Hard Success: roll ≤ 1/2 value.
• Extreme Success: roll ≤ 1/5 value.
• Critical: roll equals 01.
• Fumble: roll 96–100 (or 100 if skill is 50 or higher).
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleSuccessLevelsExample: Investigator with Spot Hidden 60 rolls 24. Since 24 is below 30 (half), it is a Hard Success.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleIdeaRollSummary: Special INT check called by the Keeper exclusively when an investigation hits a dead end.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleIdeaRollMechanics: Always yields the crucial clue needed to advance (Fail-forward). On success, the investigator connects facts instantly. On failure, the clue is revealed alongside sudden peril or lost time. Cannot be pushed or altered with Luck.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleIdeaRollExample: Players are lost on where a suspect fled. Failed Idea Roll: investigator recalls a tram ticket, but thugs immediately corner him in the alley.
CompendiumModal.lore_rulePushedRollSummary: A second attempt at a failed skill check by taking an explicit, heightened risk.
CompendiumModal.lore_rulePushedRollMechanics: The player must justify extra effort or time. Failing a pushed roll results in direct disaster (broken tool, SAN loss, arrest, injury). Combat and Sanity checks cannot be pushed.
CompendiumModal.lore_rulePushedRollExample: Failed Locksmith check. Player pushes by forcing the lock with a crowbar. Pushed failure: crowbar snaps loudly, alerting guards above.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleBonusPenaltySummary: Extra tens die rolled to represent unusually advantageous or hazardous circumstances.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleBonusPenaltyMechanics: Roll one units die and two (or more) tens dice. With a Bonus die, choose the lower (better) tens die. With a Penalty die, choose the higher (worse) tens die. Bonus and Penalty dice cancel 1:1.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleBonusPenaltyExample: Firing a revolver at a target shrouded in pitch darkness requires a penalty die.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleSanitySummary: Measurement of mental fortitude against Mythos horrors and reality-shattering truths.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleSanityMechanics: Losing 5 or more SAN in a single roll causes Temporary Insanity (bout of madness lasting 1d10 rounds). Losing 1/5 of current SAN in one in-game day triggers Indefinite Insanity (phobias, manias, amnesia). Reaching 0 SAN is permanent madness.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleSanityExample: Seeing a Shoggoth prompts a 1d6/1d20 Sanity check. Failing and rolling 14 loss causes immediate panic and amnesia.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleCombatSummary: Dynamic round-based scuffles resolved in Dexterity (DEX) order.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleCombatMechanics: A defender chooses to Fight Back or Dodge. The higher success level wins. Ties in fighting back go to the attacker. Firearms cannot be countered in hand-to-hand without special conditions.
CompendiumModal.lore_ruleCombatExample: A cultist strikes with a dagger (Regular Success). The investigator Dodges (Hard Success), cleanly slipping past the blade.
